item.title: Policy Management
item.description: What is a Speedle policy? The Policy Management Service (PMS) manages services, authorization policies, role policies and custom functions. A policy store persists those objects using a registered storage backend. Services and authorization policies A service scopes its policies. An authorization policy grants or denies a principal permission to perform an action on a resource, optionally subject to a condition. Except for global role policies, policies do not automatically apply in another service.

item.title: Usecases
item.description: Application specific policies Alex Chan is a developer who is implementing a simple application with golang. His application requires Authorization and he doesn’t want to re-invent the wheel. Alex can use an open source choice like Speedle for Authorization. Centalized policy enforcement and management Jin Chen is a security manager of multinational company. His team monitor dozens of internal systems. Different systems use different authorization mechanisms, different policy languages. They are eager to find a solution to manage all these systems efficiently.

item.title: Global Policy
item.description: When should a role be global? Ordinary roles are scoped to a service. When several services share a role assignment, define the assignment in the specially named global service and use that role in each service’s own authorization policies. Only global role policies are supported. A global role assignment does not itself grant every operation; each ordinary service still defines its permissions. Global authorization policies are not supported. Before running the examples Build .

item.title: Policy Diagnosis
item.description: What does diagnosis show? Diagnose explains an authorization evaluation: decision, reason, effective roles, attributes, and the policies examined. It accepts the same request context as IsAllowed; REST uses /authz-check/v1/diagnose, and both Go/gRPC use Diagnose. Diagnosis exposes policy definitions and request context. Restrict it to trusted operators using the API security controls; it is not a public debugging endpoint. Before running the examples Build ./bin/spctl, ./bin/speedle-pms and ./bin/speedle-ads using the quick start.

item.title: Authorization Decisions
item.description: What is an authorization decision? Speedle evaluates a subject, action and resource within a service. The application must enforce the result. Treat an evaluation error or timeout separately from a normal Deny and fail closed. REST, gRPC and embedded Go APIs have different wire representations; use their respective contracts. Before running the examples Build ./bin/spctl, ./bin/speedle-pms and ./bin/speedle-ads using the quick start. Use Go 1.26 or later, Bash, curl and Python 3.

item.title: Policy Discovery
item.description: What can discover mode do? * Help you discover existing authorization requests The is-allowed API endpoint and the discover API endpoint use the same request and response format. When you replace is-allowed with discover in the URL of the API, each authorization request that is returned shows WHO carries out WHAT action on WHICH resource. Discover mode does not evaluate the authorization decision; it simply records the authorization decision requests, along with the actions and the resources protected, and returns “is-allowed=true”.

item.title: SPDL - Speedle Policy Definition Language
item.description: Syntax Keywords grant, deny, user, group, entity, role, from, on, if and in have special meanings in their syntax positions. Statement keywords are case-insensitive. In conditions, use in or IN; function names are case-sensitive. Principal, action and resource names are also case-sensitive. The current parser accepts keyword-like names in some name positions, so a blanket prohibition is not a validation rule. Prefer unambiguous names for review and client interoperability.

item.title: Identity Domain
item.description: What is an identity domain? An identity domain (idd) is an explicit namespace for a principal. Two users named user1 can belong to different domains. The string is supplied by trusted integration code or a configured token asserter; it is not proof of authentication. Speedle does not infer or validate a provider’s tenant model merely from the domain name. Represent domains in policies and requests grant user user1 from github read book grant user user1 from IDCS.

item.title: Token asserter
item.description: What does a token asserter do? A configured asserter validates a token and returns explicit principals, including their identity domains. Speedle can then evaluate policies using those identities. A production implementation must validate the token’s signature or introspection result, issuer, audience, expiry and any provider-specific requirements. The webhook alone does not establish compatibility with arbitrary OAuth/OIDC tokens. The Token Assertion Plugin API uses integer errCode and an optional attribute object, not a typed attribute array.

item.title: API
item.description: REST APIs These are reference contracts for your configured PMS/ADS or asserter endpoint. speedle.io serves documentation and the browser Playground; it is not a hosted PMS/ADS service. Supply JSON with Content-Type: application/json, and configure TLS/mTLS and caller access controls. Policy management API Authorization decision API Token assertion webhook Policy and role-policy IDs are strings. PMS responses are flat objects; authorization permissions use permissions (plural). REST decision requests use a typed attribute array, whereas diagnostic response attributes and webhook attributes are objects.

item.title: Deployment
item.description: Deploy Speedle in embedded mode Speedle works as a Go library. To deploy Speedle in embedded mode, simply pull Speedle from the repository and import it in golang code. The Policy Management Service (PMS) golang API is called to do policy management, and the Authorization Decision Service (ADS) golang API is called to do runtime authorization checks. item.title: Pluggable Storage
item.description: Built-in stores and extension contracts The standalone binaries register file, etcd and MongoDB implementations under pkg/store. Availability does not mean identical operational guarantees; review backend authentication, persistence, transaction and watch behavior for your deployment. The configuration below illustrates property names; running etcd/MongoDB deployments is outside this local example. A full backend implements pms.PolicyStoreManager: service, authorization-policy, role-policy and function management, snapshot reads, health checks, watch/stop, and close. ADS accepts the narrower PolicyStoreManagerADS read/watch interface.

item.title: Security
item.description: Protect both API transports Speedle’s standalone PMS and ADS expose REST and gRPC. Both now use the same --insecure, --cert, --key, --client-cert and --force-client-cert transport settings. Invalid certificates or trust configuration cause startup to fail; secure mode does not fall back to plaintext. TLS encrypts the connection and authenticates the server. To require authenticated clients, provide a client CA with --client-cert and set --force-client-cert=true. Without that flag, a configured CA validates a client certificate only when the client supplies one.

item.title: Versions
item.description: Current development documentation These pages describe the current master source, not a frozen historical release. The current module requires Go 1.26 or later. The quick-start workflow verifies Go 1.26.10 and 1.27.3; those tested patch versions are not a promise that an old release has the same requirements. When upgrading, review the chosen commit and dependencies and repeat the integration checks for your store, transport and identity provider. Current standalone gRPC uses the same TLS/mTLS settings as REST and inherits its listening host unless --grpc-endpoint is supplied.

item.title: Custom Function
item.description: Why use a custom function? SPDL conditions can call a configured function when built-in operators or functions do not express the required rule. Speedle calls its REST endpoint with POST {"params":[...]} and expects {"result":...} or {"error":"..."}. Parameter order/types and the result type must match the condition. Function failures are evaluation errors; applications must fail closed. Start the local example This example accepts numeric values from 100 to 50000. Wrong parameter types or an empty parameter list return an HTTP error.
